User guide

Getting started

This page takes you from an empty window to an exported MP4. For installation see the Install in the README.

The window

  • Media bin (left): every file, generator and reel of the project, with thumbnails and durations. Cards can be grouped and locked.
  • Preview (centre) with the level meters and master fader on the right. Under it: the project frame rate, the preview resolution, the pitch engine and the preview quality.
  • Timeline (bottom): the ruler with markers and the region, then the tracks — video first, then audio, then morph tracks. Track headers carry mute (M), solo (S) and lock.
  • Toolbar (under the timeline): transport, timecode, speed, and the editing buttons — markers, adding tracks, split, copy/paste, delete, trims, zoom, region, loop, undo, render, search and diagnostics.
  • Status line (bottom): zoom, region, cache, underruns, shown video fps, and on the right the hint for whatever is under the mouse.

A first edit

  1. Add media. Drop video or audio files on the window: a file dropped on the timeline lands where you drop it, a file dropped on the bin becomes a card you can drag in later. A video with sound arrives as a linked pair — a video event and an audio event that move together.
  2. Play. Tap Space to play and pause; hold Space to speed up towards 4×. Click the ruler to move the playhead; A/D (or Home/End) jump to the previous/next marker, region or event edge.
  3. Cut. Put the playhead where the cut goes and press S. Drag events to move them; drag their edges to trim. Dragging an event onto its neighbour makes a crossfade.
  4. Add effects. Double-click an event to open its effects window and press + effect… — see Effects and automation.
  5. Mark a region. Drag on the ruler, or press I and O at the start and end. L loops it.
  6. Save. Ctrl+S writes a .kt project file. Autosave keeps a recovery copy in the background; File → Recover unsaved work… brings it back after a crash.
  7. Render. File → Render to MP4… — see Export and kt-cli.

Projects

File → New and File → Open… work with .kt projects. Files from other programs (.otio) and from older Kinetren versions (.ktproj) come in through File → Import older Kinetren project…, which creates a new project and leaves the original untouched. File → Project settings… sets frame rate, size and the rule for fitting sources of another size (fit with transparent borders, fill, stretch, or as is).

Language

View → Language switches between English, Spanish, Simplified Chinese, Russian and Arabic; Auto follows the system.
